definition: Very attentive to detail and hard to please about standards.
example: A fastidious host polished every glass before the guests arrived.
nuance: Fastidious can imply demanding standards, especially of cleanliness, taste, or accuracy.
prompt: An editor insists that every citation follow the style guide exactly.
options: The fastidious editor checked every reference and rejected even minor inconsistencies.
The fastidious editor finished quickly by ignoring small inconsistencies.
His fastidious response arrived sooner than anyone expected.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: very attentive to detail and hard to please about standards.
Ignoring details conflicts with exacting standards.
Fastidious is not related to being fast.
